newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade Bourse turnover down week ending Sept 6.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade Bourse turnover down week ending Sept 6.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) on Monday reported a drop in turnover to 46.258 million dinars in the week ending September 6 from 60.912 million the previous week.
The number of transactions rose by only one, to 185.
"The high turnover in the week ending August 30 was primarily due to high volume of central bank bonds traded," Milko Stimac of the BSE told Reuters.
Although trading in central bank bonds was down to 23.51 million dinars in five transactions last week from 37.23 million in 10 deals the previous week, they still accounted for most of the turnover.
Trading in commercial paper dropped to 19.358 million dinars in 157 deals from the previous week's 20.547 million in 159 transactions.
Interest rates on these securities ranged from 44 to 520 percent per year and maturity from seven to 30 days.

The most actively traded commercial bills were those issued by chemicals producer Hipol (2.558 million dinars), food processor BIM Slavija (2.035 million), Karic Bank (1.44 million) and AIK Bank Senta (1.255 million).

"Summer months are generally slower and we expect a seasonal revival of market movements and turnover to increase in the next few weeks of September," Stimac said. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 2224305
